options.content: The receiver's response to the message
options.rationale: Correct: it shows whether the message was understood.

options.content: The channel used to send the message
options.rationale: That is the medium.

options.content: The person who starts the message
options.rationale: That is the sender.

options.content: Noise that interrupts the message
options.rationale: That is a barrier.

explanation: **Feedback** is the receiver's response, which makes communication two-way.

stem: Which is an example of external communication?

options.content: A letter from a business to a supplier
options.rationale: Correct: the supplier is outside the business.

options.content: A memo from a manager to staff
options.rationale: Memos are internal.

options.content: A notice on the staff noticeboard
options.rationale: Notices to staff are internal.

options.content: A meeting of the sales department
options.rationale: Department meetings are internal.

explanation: **External** communication is with people outside the business: customers, suppliers, banks, government.

stem: A machine has broken down and the factory manager must contact the repair company immediately. Which method is most suitable?

options.content: Letter by post
options.rationale: Post is far too slow for an emergency.

options.content: Telephone call
options.rationale: Correct: fast and two-way for an urgent problem.

options.content: Notice on the factory board
options.rationale: A notice is internal and does not reach the repairer.

options.content: Written report
options.rationale: A report takes time to prepare.

explanation: When a message is **urgent**, a fast two-way method such as a **phone call** is best.

stem: A business must confirm the terms of a contract with a customer. Which method is most suitable?

options.content: A telephone call only
options.rationale: A call leaves no written record.

options.content: A face-to-face chat only
options.rationale: A chat leaves no evidence of the terms.

options.content: A notice in the shop window
options.rationale: A notice is public and not personal.

options.content: A letter or email
options.rationale: Correct: it gives a permanent written record.

explanation: When a **record** is needed, use written communication such as a letter or email.

stem: Which is a disadvantage of email?

options.content: It is always slower than sending a letter
options.rationale: Email is usually much faster than post.

options.content: It may be ignored or lost among many other messages
options.rationale: Correct: busy receivers may not read it.

options.content: It cannot carry attached documents
options.rationale: Email can carry attachments.

options.content: It leaves no record of the message
options.rationale: Emails can be stored as records.

explanation: Email is fast, cheap and leaves a record, but it needs internet access and may be **ignored or missed**.

stem: Which is the main advantage of a meeting over a notice?

options.content: It leaves a permanent written record automatically
options.rationale: A notice is written; a meeting needs minutes for a record.

options.content: Questions can be asked and answered immediately
options.rationale: Correct: meetings allow two-way communication.

options.content: It costs nothing in staff time
options.rationale: Meetings use a lot of staff time.

options.content: It reaches people who are absent
options.rationale: Absent people miss meetings.

explanation: Meetings give **immediate feedback**; notices are one-way.

stem: A manager wants to show staff how sales changed over twelve months. Which method makes the pattern easiest to understand quickly?

options.content: A long written report with no charts
options.rationale: Text makes trends harder to see.

options.content: A telephone call to each employee
options.rationale: Figures are hard to follow by phone.

options.content: A line graph
options.rationale: Correct: visual communication shows trends at a glance.

options.content: A text message listing all the figures
options.rationale: A list of numbers is hard to read on a phone.

explanation: **Visual** methods such as graphs and charts make numerical patterns easy to understand.

stem: A manager must tell an employee privately that he is receiving a formal warning. Which is the best approach?

options.content: A notice on the staff noticeboard
options.rationale: This breaks confidentiality.

options.content: A message in the staff group chat
options.rationale: Everyone in the group would see it.

options.content: A private meeting followed by a letter
options.rationale: Correct: confidential, two-way and recorded.

options.content: Announcing it at a staff meeting
options.rationale: This would embarrass the employee publicly.

explanation: **Confidential** matters need a private method; a letter provides the **record**.
hints: The message is confidential and must be recorded.

stem: A notice on a staff noticeboard is an example of one-way communication.
explanation: True. No immediate feedback is expected.

stem: Email can only be used for internal communication.
explanation: False. Email is used both within a business and with customers, suppliers and others outside it.

stem: Match each situation with the most suitable method of communication.

left.content: Telling all 200 workers about a public holiday
Discussing a new product idea with five managers
Sending a detailed price list to a customer in Zambia
Asking a nearby supplier whether stock is available today

explanation: The best method depends on the number of receivers, the need for discussion, distance and urgency.

stem: A shop wants to tell 180 regular customers about a sale. Sending a letter costs US\$2.40 each, including printing and postage. Calculate the total cost of sending letters.
explanation: 180 × US\$2.40 = US\$432. Email or a messaging app would cost almost nothing, which is why cost is a key factor in choosing a method.
workedSolution: 1. 180 × US\$2.40 = US\$432. Email or a messaging app would cost almost nothing, which is why cost is a key factor in choosing a method.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why effective communication is important to a business.

points.description: Instructions understood / work coordinated.
Fewer mistakes and less waste.
Motivation / customer relationships / decision-making / records.
Explains the second reason.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Clear communication means employees understand their instructions, so work is coordinated and fewer mistakes are made. Good communication with customers, such as answering enquiries quickly, builds relationships and keeps them buying.

explanation: Importance: instructions, decisions, motivation, relationships, promotion, records, trade.

stem: Explain **two** ways information and communication technology has changed communication in small enterprises.

points.description: Faster and cheaper communication (messaging apps, email).
Enterprises reach suppliers and customers instantly at low cost.
Social media marketing / mobile money / online orders / computer records.
Explains the effect, e.g. wider market reached cheaply.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Mobile phones and messaging apps let small enterprises contact suppliers and customers instantly and cheaply, instead of travelling. Social media allows a small business to advertise to many potential customers at almost no cost, widening its market.

explanation: ICT impact: speed, low cost, wider markets, electronic payments, records; problems include cost of data, power cuts and cyber-crime.
hints: Think about phones and the internet.

stem: Gweru Furnishers (a fictional business) has 64 employees working in three shops. The owner wants to tell all staff that the shops will open on Sundays from next month, and that Sunday work will be paid at a higher rate. A text message costs about US\$0.03 per person to send.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of sending one text message to every employee.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Is this message internal or external communication, and why?

options.content: External, because staff work in three different shops
options.rationale: All three shops belong to the same business.

options.content: External, because a mobile phone network is used
options.rationale: The channel does not decide whether it is internal.

options.content: Internal, because it is sent by text message
options.rationale: The method does not decide; the receivers do.

options.content: Internal, because it is sent to the business's own staff
options.rationale: Correct: staff are inside the business.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of using text messages for this announcement.

points.description: Advantage: fast / cheap / reaches all three shops at once.
Explains with the case (e.g. under US\$2 for all staff).
Disadvantage: no chance to ask questions / may be missed / too short to explain pay rates.
Explains why this matters for a change to working days.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Text messages reach all 64 staff in three shops at once for about US\$1.92, so it is very fast and cheap. However, a short text cannot explain the new pay rate fully or allow staff to ask questions, and some staff may be unhappy about working on Sundays.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Recommend the best way for the owner to communicate this change. Justify your answer.

points.description: Recommends a method or combination (e.g. meeting in each shop + written notice/letter).
Justifies: change affects working conditions; staff need to ask questions (feedback).
Justifies: written record of new pay rate and days.
Explains why an alternative alone is less suitable.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The owner should hold a short meeting in each shop to explain the Sunday opening and the higher pay, so staff can ask questions and raise concerns, followed by a written notice or letter setting out the new days and pay rate. Because the change affects working conditions, staff need both the chance to discuss it and a written record. A text message alone is too short and gives no chance for discussion.

explanation: (a) 64 × US\$0.03 = US\$1.92. (b) Internal. (c) Fast and cheap, but no feedback. (d) Meeting plus written confirmation.
hints: (a) Cost per person × number of employees.
(d) Does the message need feedback, a record, or both?

stem: Chipo runs a small catering business in Harare that prepares food for weddings and company events. She receives enquiries by phone, email and through her social media page, and she sends quotations to customers. Last month two customers complained that they had agreed a different price by phone from the one on their invoice.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Explain **two** advantages to Chipo of using social media to communicate with customers.

points.description: Reaches many potential customers cheaply.
Can show photographs of her food (visual), attracting bookings.
Two-way: customers can ask questions and leave reviews.
Good reviews build trust with new customers.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Social media lets Chipo reach many potential customers at little cost and show photographs of her food, which attracts bookings. It is two-way, so customers can ask questions and leave good reviews that build trust with new customers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Recommend how Chipo should communicate prices to customers to avoid further complaints. Justify your answer.

points.description: Problem: phone agreements leave no record.
Recommends written quotations (email / letter / message) for every price.
Customer confirms in writing before the event.
Phone still useful for quick discussion, followed by written confirmation.
Considers cost/time of extra paperwork vs benefit.
Justified recommendation.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The complaints happened because prices agreed by phone left no record. Chipo should keep using the phone for quick discussions, but always follow up with a written quotation by email or message showing the menu, number of guests and price, and ask the customer to confirm in writing. This takes a little more time, but both sides then have the same record, so invoices will match what was agreed and disputes can be settled quickly. Written confirmation is the most important change, because it removes the cause of the complaints.

explanation: Social media is cheap and visual; prices need written communication to provide a record.
